items.q: A new product development project: Year 0 revenue £0, cost £8,000. Year 1 revenue £4,000, cost £1,000. Year 2 revenue £6,000, cost £1,600. Year 3 revenue £4,350, cost £1,290. Calculate the average rate of return (ARR).
items.label: Paper 1 June 2026 Q16

items.q: The chart shows a business's inventory over time. Deliveries arrive instantly at the end of a day. What is the re-order quantity?
items.why: Each delivery lifts inventory from the buffer level of 200 units to the maximum of 300 units, so the re-order quantity is 300 – 200 = 100 units.

items.q: Kempshott plc: actual output 52 units, selling price £16,000 per unit, variable costs £7,000 per unit, fixed costs £360,000. Calculate its margin of safety.
items.why: Contribution per unit = £16,000 – £7,000 = £9,000. Break-even = £360,000 ÷ £9,000 = 40 units. Margin of safety = 52 – 40 = 12 units. The answer is in units.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2026 Q17

items.q: A factory can produce 9,000 units a month. It produced 5,600 units last month. What is its capacity utilisation?
items.why: Capacity utilisation = actual output ÷ maximum possible output × 100 = 5,600 ÷ 9,000 × 100 = 62.2%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company has non-current liabilities of £80m and total equity of £280m. What is its gearing?
items.why: Capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities = £280m + £80m = £360m. Gearing = non-current liabilities ÷ capital employed × 100 = 80 ÷ 360 × 100 = 22.2%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A retailer has revenue of £765,000, cost of sales of £510,000 and average inventory of £145,000. What is its inventory turnover?
items.why: Inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory = £510,000 ÷ £145,000 = 3.5 times a year.
items.label: New question

items.q: Revenue £25,750m. Gross profit margin 24.5%. Gross profit = ?
items.why: Gross profit = Revenue x Gross profit margin = 25,750 x 0.245 = £6,308.75m. Simple calculation: multiply revenue by the margin percentage.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business has 90 employees who are each expected to work 230 days a year. 450 working days were lost to absence. What is the absenteeism rate?
items.why: Absenteeism = days lost ÷ total possible working days × 100 = 450 ÷ (90 × 230) × 100 = 450 ÷ 20,700 × 100 = 2.17%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has capacity utilisation of 80%. It increases its capacity by 25% while output stays the same. What is its new capacity utilisation?
items.why: Take capacity as 100 units: output is 80. New capacity = 125. Utilisation = 80 ÷ 125 × 100 = 64%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business sells 8,500 units at £14 each. Variable cost is £10 per unit and fixed costs are £20,000. What is its profit?
items.why: Total contribution = (£14 – £10) × 8,500 = £34,000. Profit = total contribution – fixed costs = £34,000 – £20,000 = £14,000.
items.label: New question
